Commentary.Commentary: The Irish bowling in general wasn't up to the mark but the likes of Tim Murtagh, Peter Chase and Barry McCarthy impressed time and again. The target is a big one and the visiting team will have to bat extremely well to pose any threat. Do join us in a short while for the chase.

After put into bat, England started decently. Jason Roy struggled but Alex Hales was timing his shots brilliantly. Once the opening partnership was broken, the most experienced pair of Morgan and Root got together to raise a 140-run stand. It provided a good base for the late order hitting although Ireland showed signs of coming back. They picked up three wickets in quick time to stifle the proceedings a bit but then Bairstow and Rashid exploded to spoil all their good work.

Great finishing touch provided by the pair of Jonny Bairstow and Adil Rashid. The innings seemed to be losing its way at the back end but they made sure it remained on track and powered the final total beyond the 300-run mark.

FOUR! Finishes with a flourish! Fullish delivery on middle and leg, Bairstow clears his front leg and whips it over front of square on the leg side. Has hit it well and the ball rolls away to the fence. ENGLAND END UP WITH 328/6.

SIX! Bairstow has given the much-needed momentum at the fag end of the innings! Short delivery around off and it sits up nicely for Bairstow. He pulls hard over deep mid-wicket and the ball clears the fence with ease.
Full delivery outside off, Willey drills it to long off for a single.
David Willey is in next.

OUT! A handy cameo from Rashid comes to an end! Short of a length ball around the hips, Rashid looks to pick it up over the fielder at short fine leg but only manages to get a top edge. The ball spoons towards the left of Niall O'Brien behind the stumps who takes a regulation catch.
FOUR! Another short delivery on off, Rashid goes for a pull over mid on and just manages to clear the fielder inside the ring to get the desired result.
Short delivery and it's climbing up on Rashid. He miscues his pull to deep mid-wicket. Two runs taken.
Peter Chase is back on.
SIX! Bang! Fullish on middle and leg, Jonny whips it over deep mid-wicket. Has generated a lot of power and gets a maximum to his name.
Full delivery outside off, Bairstow looks to carve it over covers but misses.
SIX! Boom! In the slot outside off, Bairstow clubs it over long on and the ball clears the fence with ease.
Another one in the blockhole outside off, this time he fails to get any bat on it.
4th ODI fifty for Jonny Bairstow!
FOUR! Yorker outside off, Bairstow looks to carve it away but gets a bottom edge that beats short third man and runs to the fence. It has been a really good knock from him.
On a length outside off, Rashid mistimes it through mid off for a single.
Barry McCarthy is back on.
The batsman guides it to point. They pick up a single. Big over for the hosts.
FOUR! This is good batting from Rashid! On a length on off, he backs away and lofts it over covers for a boundary.

FOUR! Fullish delivery on middle and leg, Rashid whips it over mid-wicket. McCarthy sprints to his right and slides to keep the ball in play. The umpires go upstairs to check for the boundary and it is one as his foot touched the ropes while in contact with the ball.

Brilliant effort, Dockrell! Short delivery on middle and leg, Bairstow hooks it uppishly towards Dockrell at long leg. He judges it well, moves back and leaps to grab it. He realizes that the momentum will take him over the ropes. So he flicks the ball in play as he crosses the fence. What presence of mind from him! The umpires check whether he stepped on the fence while in contact with the ball but he is fine. Saves a run for his side.
FOUR! Elegant! Full length ball outside off, Bairstow goes inside out over covers and does it beautifully to find the fence.
On a length outside off, drilled to sweeper cover for a single.
Kevin O'Brien is back on.
On a length wide outside off, Jonny throws his bat at it but gets a bottom edge towards the keeper.
FOUR! Low full toss on off, Bairstow whips it over mid-wicket and in the process his bottom hand comes off the handle. Still he has generated enough power on it to beat the man in the deep.
Jonny drills it to extra cover and sets off. A misfield by the fielder allows the batsmen to take the extra run.
Wider outside off, Bairstow reaches out to it and slices it over backward point. Two runs taken.
On a length and angling into Rashid. He slogs it to long on for a run.
Slower and full around off, Bairstow kneels and sweeps it to deep mid-wicket for a single.
Tim Murtagh comes back for a bowl.

Short delivery and it's climbing on Rashid. He pulls it but not with much control to deep mid-wicket. The batsmen turn back for the second and Adil has to dive in desperately as the throw is an accurate one at the keeper's end. Two runs taken.
Slower and full delivery outside off, Rashid looks to drive it with an open face but fails to get any bat on it.
Leg bye! Angling in towards the pads, Jonny fails to play it across but is hit on the pads and the ball rolls to covers. A leg bye taken.
Good length ball outside off, driven hard through point for a single.
Back of a length outside off, Rashid looks to run it down to third man. Wrong shot selection and he gets beaten.
Short delivery on middle and leg, pulled down to fine leg for a single.

Peter Chase comes back for his final over. This is the 20th bowling change of the innings, informs one of the commentators on air. Shows the Irish skipper William Porterfield has been quite active, not sure if proactive as he let the game drift away when the partnership between Eoin Morgan and Joe Root was growing.
Full and outside off, Rashid plays it in the air over covers, not much timing but it falls safely in the deep. A couple again. 12 from the over!
Lands it full and outside off, an off-pace delivery, Jonny pushes it to long off for one.
Fullish and on middle, Bairstow drills it down the ground and the long on fielder makes a sliding stop. A couple of runs taken.
Rashid  plays it with an angled bat and guides it to third man. One run added to the total.

FOUR! Good shot! A leg stump half-volley this time, Rashid whips it across the line and sends it right through the gap between deep mid-wicket and deep square leg for a boundary. Bisecting the fielders superbly.
A juicy half-volley outside off, it's driven through covers for a couple of runs.
Barry McCarthy returns for a bowl.
Loopy and on middle, Adil tickles it off his pads to short fine leg where the fielder makes a diving stop. A single taken to end the over.
Goes hard at it and punches it to sweeper cover for one.
Flighted on middle, turned through backward square leg for a single.
Flicks it to deep square leg for a run.
FOUR! Nicely played! Flatter and shorter outside off, Bairstow goes deep inside the crease and cuts it behind point for a boundary.
The batsman has played it fine down the leg side. A single taken.
FOUR! Deft! Murtagh offers width outside off with third man inside the ring, all Bairstow needs to do is find the gap square of the wicket on the off side. He does that and fetches a boundary.
Rashid opens the face of the bat and helps it to third man. The batsmen have run through for a single.
EDGY FOUR! Murtagh serves it on a length and just outside off, Rashid tries to defend close to his body but gets a big fat edge down to third man for a boundary.
Full and on off, Adil pushes it off his front foot to mid on.
A touch short in length and around middle, Jonny works it in front of square leg and picks up a single.
Angles in a full ball on off, Rashid plays it with soft hands and drops it adjacent to the pitch. He calls his partner through for a quick single. Well judged!
Tim Murtagh is back on.
Flighted and around leg, skidding down, Rashid fails to flick and they cross for a leg bye.
Adil Rashid is the new man in.

OUT! Another wicket goes down and Ireland are doing a really good job at the back end of this innings. Dockrell serves it full and outside off, Billings runs down the track probably with the intention of going big over mid-wicket. But he ends up playing it in the air towards long on. Kevin O'Brien in the deep runs across to his left and completes the catch easily. Good phase of play for the Irish!
The batsman has played it to the point region. One run added to the total.
Sliding down the leg side, Jonny nudges it through mid-wicket and scampers back for the second run.
On the pads, Bairstow fails to keep it out.
Full and around leg, this is the fourth time, I guess Bairstow has played the sweep shot but fails to find the gap. Straight to short fine leg.
Pitches it full and on off, Jonny drives it through mid off for a single.
Short and outside off, cut straight to point.
Played to the point region by the batsman. No run.
Uses his wrists this time to force a full ball down to long on for a run.
FOUR! Fabulous! On a length and outside off, Sam gets forward to drive it on the up. The connection is crisp and it speeds through extra cover for a delightful boundary.
Good length ball angling into the batsman, Billings tries playing it straight but misses and is hit on the thigh pad.
Peter Chase is back on as well.
Time for the Powerplay. Maximum of five fielders allowed outside the ring now.
Tossed up around middle and leg, Bairstow sweeps it but it is straight to the man at short fine leg. End of a tidy over from Dockrell.
This time he whips it nicely to deep mid-wicket and picks up two runs for it.
Bairstown runs down the track and looks to whip it across. Only manages to get an inside edge to short fine leg.
Stays back and punches this one down to long on for a run.
Fires this one in seeing Billings giving the charge. He misses his flick to get rapped on the pads.

A good shout for an LBW turned down! Tosses this one nicely just outside off, coming in with the arm. Bairstow kneels, looks to sweep it hard but misses to get rapped on the pads and the ball rolls to the leg side. However, the umpire is not interested in the appeal and turns it down. The batsmen steal a leg bye. The replays show that it was umpire's call, so turns out to be fair.
Wide! Slips this one down the leg side, Bairstow looks to sweep it but fails to make any contact.
George Dockrell to bowl now.
Back of a length delivery outside off, Bairstow places it through cover-point for a run. Successful over for Ireland, a wicket and two runs from it.
On a good length outside off, Billings punches it through covers for a run and gets off the mark.
An attempted slower delivery which turns out to be a low full toss outside off, dabbed to point.
Billings again moves across and turns this one to mid-wicket.
Straightway shuffles across and defends the fullish delivery to mid on.
Sam Billings is the new batsman.

OUT! Big wicket for Ireland! He could have been dangerous if he stayed till the slog overs. Morgan backs away a bit, uses his feet in search to open up the off side. McCarthy smartly bowls the slower delivery on a good length on off and it cuts back in. The English skipper doesn't have much pace to work with. Ends up chipping it towards short extra cover where Ed Joyce dives full length to his right to take a fine catch. Barry has been brilliant today and gets his second wicket.
Barry McCarthy is back on.
Angling into Jonny. He tucks it through backward square leg and runs two runs for it.
Overpitched delivery outside off, carved through point for a single.
A bit of room on offer this time, placed behind point for a couple this time.
Angling in from outside off, there is not much room to work with as it is chopped to point.
Length delivery on middle and leg, Morgan whips it to mid-wicket. Didn't get much timing on that.
Fullish delivery outside off, driven crisply to extra cover.
Wide! Starts off with a loosener down the leg side, Morgan fails to glance it but a good take by the keeper.
Kevin O'Brien is back on.
Slower delivery outside off, eased through mid off for a single.
Fullish delivery angling into Morgan. Pushed off the inner half back to the bowler.
On a good length on off, Bairstow plays it with soft hands towards mid on and steals a single.
Back of a length ball, turned to square leg.
FOUR! Well played! On a fuller length around off, Jonny drives it straight and on the up. No chance for the bowler to stop it and the ball whistles away to the fence.
On a good length outside off, stroked past the extra cover fielder. Bairstow wants the single but Morgan sends him back.
Back of a length ball on middle and leg, worked to deep mid-wicket for a single. Only a run and the precious wicket of Root. Great stuff from Chase.
Bairstow turns this one to mid-wicket.
Bairstow shuffles a touch and pushes it towards Chase who stops it in his followthrough.
Short of a length just outside off, Bairstow is opened up in his stance a bit but does well to tap it towards point.

Jonny Bairstow walks in next. He recently scored a 113-ball 174 in a List A game against Durham and is pushing for a regular spot in England's playing XI in ODIs. Once the players like Chris Woakes, Jos Buttler and Ben Stokes will return, it's quite difficult to break in. Should look to make most of the opportunity at hand.

OUT! Joe Root departs against the run of play! Good length delivery outside off, Root chips down the track and looks to go downtown. Hits it well but doesn't get the required elevation on it and the ball flies towards Andrew Balbirnie at mid off. He pouches it safely. End of a brilliant 140-run stand. Can the tourists keep on chipping away at the wickets and slow down the scoring rate from here on?
Chase runs in hard and tails in a fullish delivery into Root. He looks to play it across but gets a feather nick on to his pads. A stifled appeal for an LBW is turned down.
Peter Chase is back on.
Length and around off, Root heaves it in front of square leg and collects a single. Big applause from the knowledgeable Lord's crowd as 200 comes up for England.
Another slower delivery, an off cutter outside off, Root works it around but finds the mid-wicket fielder.
Slower short ball around off, Morgan is two feet in the air as he tries to dominate the bounce. Does well to keep his pull shot down and sends it through square leg for a run.
Good length ball on off, not much width on offer, Root can only play it straight and he pushes it through mid on for a run.
Full and around off, Root easily flicks it through mid-wicket and gathers a couple of runs.
Slightly short and around off, Root goes back and punches it through covers for a couple.
Tim Murtagh returns for another spell. He got the ball to move early on in the innings and troubled the batsmen. Can he generate some reverse swing now?

Time for Drinks. Joe Root and Eoin Morgan continue to dominate the proceedings and things are looking gloomy for the visitors at the moment. They need to find a wicket from somewhere or else a score above 350 is on the cards with the firepower the English batting possesses.

FOUR! Well played! Once again after conceding a boundary, Kevin overdoes his length. Goes short as a follow-up delivery around off and Morgan brings out his lethal pull shot. Dismisses it through the leg side and the mid-wicket fielder fails to cut it off after covering good ground to his left. 14 from the over, 27 in last three, England looking to up the scoring rate now.

FOUR! Eoin decides to open his arms. The fuller length ball around off gives him the opportunity to do so and he smashes it over mid off for a boundary. The fielder was inside the ring and hence it was a risk worth taking.
Angles in a full ball on off, from around the wicket, Morgan pushes it back to the bowler.
Kevin overdoes his length, bowls it full and straight, it's easily flicked through mid-wicket for a single.
The on air commentators feel that even a score above 300 on a good track like this doesn't guarantee that you are safe. One isn't really sure what is a match-winning score on this surface...
FOUR! Root finds the gap! He receives a short ball outside off, Joe uses the pace and plays a late cut through the gap between short third man and backward point.
Short and wide outside off, Morgan forces it through covers and collects a single.
Kevin O'Brien comes back for a bowl.
Once again Morgan has to make room for himself by going back as he punches it down to long on for a run. Impressive over by Barry!
Morgan gives the charge and McCarthy follows him thereby not offering much width. The English skipper mistimes his flat-batted shot to cover-point.
Angles in a length ball on off, Morgan once again plays from the crease to the off side.
Shortish on off, Morgan goes back and defends it towards mid on.
The batsman plays the pull shot. They pick up a single.
On the pads, helped to fine leg for one.

FOUR! As a result of the previous boundary, Stirling cuts down on his length, Root has played enough cricket to sense that early, goes deep inside the crease and hammer-pulls it through mid-wicket for back-to-back boundaries. 10 from the over!
FOUR! Shot! Flighted and outside off, Root shimmies down the track and plays a bottom hand heavy drive through covers for a cracking boundary.
Knocks a full ball down to long on for a run.
Shorter delivery, Morgan fails to middle his attempted pull shot and under edges it. That stayed low.
Walks down the track and pushes it down to long on for one.
Very full and around off, Root reverse sweeps it straight to short third man.
On a length and outside off, Root works it down to third man for a single.
Slower delivery, full and angling down the leg side, Eoin eases it to fine leg for one.
Full again, on middle, Morgan tries repeating the last shot but this time he is late in closing the face of the bat. Ends up pushing it back to the bowler.
Fuller and on middle, flicked to deep mid-wicket, the longer part of the ground and returned for the second run.
An off pace delivery outside off, Morgan mistimes his drive to covers.
Full and angling into the batsman from around off, Morgan plays it on the leg side but the short mid-wicket fielder makes a fine diving stop.
Barry McCarthy is back on.
On a good length outside off, dabbed neatly to short third man for a run and Morgan will retain the strike.

FOUR!  Nicely done! In the zone outside off, Morgan drives it past the outstretched hand of Kevin and gets it past mid off for a boundary. He is oozing confidence at the moment. 100-run stand comes up!
Full length delivery outside off, Morgan mistimes his drive towards the bowler who stops it in his followthrough.
Fullish delivery, driven through mid on for a single.
Short of a length ball on off, angling in. Pushed off the inner half past the left side of the bowler. A run taken.
Fractionally overpitched outside off, driven crisply to extra cover.
32nd ODI fifty for Eoin Morgan!
Now, Morgan gets to his half century. Good show from him as well. Turns this tossed up delivery from outside off to the leg side and runs one.
21st ODI fifty for Joe Root!
Sliding in towards the pads, worked to deep mid-wicket for a single. It has been a measured knock from Root, very well deserved.
Tossed up outside off, Morgan uses his wrists and creams it to sweeper cover for a single.
Flatter delivery outside off, chopped to point.
Tossed up delivery, clipped against the spin to deep mid-wicket for a single.
Fullish delivery on middle, eased down to long on for a single.
FOUR! Well played! Shortish delivery outside off, this time Root has width on offer. Spanks it through point for a boundary. 150 up for England!
Back of a length delivery angling into Root. He was looking to open up the off side but doesn't have enough room to work with. Plays it away to point.
Good length delivery on off, stays low. Root is surprised by the lack of bounce but manages to keep it out.
Stays back to the similar length delivery and eases it to mid on.
On a length on off, whipped but straight to the man at mid-wicket.
Angling into Morgan. Clipped to deep square leg for a run.
Kevin O'Brien is back for another spell.
Good fielding, Stirling. Shorter in length outside off, Root stays back and places it towards point. Stirling dives to his right and makes a brilliant stop.

FOUR! Nice improvisation! Slow through the air around off, Root has a lot of time to line it up. Goes for the fancy reverse scoop and executes it well. It goes over the keeper's head and runs down to the third man fence.
Morgan stays back to this one and works it through backward square leg for a run.
Short this time, skidding in. Root whips it to deep mid-wicket for a single.
A touch short outside off, steered past the keeper for a single.
Well bowled! Slow through the air outside off, inviting Morgan for an audacious stroke. He looks to cream it through covers but gets beaten.
George Dockrell is back into the attack.
Shorter in length outside off, Root places it uppishly through the vacant point region. Till the time the fielder in the deep cuts it off, the batsmen come back for two.
Tossed up outside off, eased down to long off for a run.
Slow through the air on middle, turned with soft hands to mid-wicket.
Morgan sits back and cuts it past the extra cover fielder. Gets two runs for doing so.
Fullish on middle and leg, clipped through mid-wicket for a single.
Tossed up around off, skidding in. Punched nicely off the back foot to sweeper cover for a single.

Good reply by Nasser Hussain! He was asked - Is Joe Root the best batsman when it comes to playing late square of the wicket? Nasser replies cheekily, if I'm in England, it's Joe, if it's India, I would say Kohli and AB de Villiers if in South Africa. Haha, we love you, Nass.
FOUR! Glorious! Fullish and on middle, Root gets behind the line and lofts it with nonchalance over the bowler's head for a boundary. Good end to the over!
Back of a length delivery outside off, Root fails to connect with his square cut this time.
Short and wide outside off, Root plays a cracking square cut but once again finds the point fielder.
Back of a length delivery on off, Root stays back and taps it down to backward point.
Gets across the stumps and punches it through covers for a run.
Fuller and outside off, stroked through covers for a single.

Almost a wicket! Quicker one, fired down the leg side, Morgan moves back to hit it through mid-wicket but misses. It goes off his pads and trickles onto the stumps. It's too slow and hence the bails don't come off. Lucky, Moggie! But had he got out, it would have been one of the unluckiest dismissals.
Walks forward and works it with the spin to deep mid-wicket for a run.
Serves a slider around off, skidding in, Morgan goes deep inside the crease and punches it through covers for a single.
Too full in length on off, forced down through mid on for a single.
Floated full ball on off, Morgan quietly plays it in the vast gap at mid-wicket and crosses for a single.
Starts from around the wicket and serves a flighted full ball on off, it's pushed back to the bowler off the front foot.
Paul Stirling has come into the attack. The Irishmen need wickets to keep the run flow in check. Can he break this threatening partnership?
Width on offer outside off, Morgan runs it down to third man and takes a single.

Chase changes his angle and digs in a short ball, well-directed, Morgan sways away at the last moment and loses his balance a bit as well. This one is more like it from "a pacer". Test him with the shorter stuff and try to expose him. Just going through the motion won't help Ireland's cause here as eventually England will run away with a big total on the board. Try and make things happen, rather waiting for it. You don't often get the chance to play at the Lord's. Make it count.
Short of a length delivery outside off, Root rises on his back foot and slaps it through cover-point for a run.
Serves it on a length around off, Root tries to tap and run but it goes quickly to the fielder and he aborts the idea.
Around off on a good length, Root stays back in defense.
Shortish and outside off, Morgan punches it to deep cover for one.
Peter Chase returns for another spell.
Fuller length ball shaping back into the batsman, Root inside edges his attempted cover drive and it rolls back towards the bowler.
Turns it off his pads to the leg side but finds short mid-wicket where Stirling makes a fine stop.
Fullish and outside off, driven through covers for a couple of runs.
Sharp short ball angling into the batsman, Root under edges his attempted pull shot onto the thigh pad.
On a length around off, Root walks down the track and mistimes his shot to mid off.
On a good length and around off, Root punches it off his back foot to mid off.
Tossed up delivery on middle, whipped to deep mid-wicket for another run. 9 from the over, going has been pretty easy for England.
Shorter in length around off, Morgan makes room and slaps it through covers for one.
The batsman works it down the leg side. They pick up a single.
Flattish and shortish again, around middle, Morgan forces it down to long on for a run.
Shortish on off, punched to sweeper cover for one.
50-run stand up for Eoin Morgan and Joe Root.
FOUR! Fine shot! Flighted full ball landing on middle and leg, Root kneels and sweeps it sweetly through backward square leg for a boundary. A handy partnership, this!
Leg bye! Angling into the pads, Joe looks to play it across but the ball brushes his pads and goes to the leg side. A leg bye taken.
Short of a length outside off, Root punches it over the leaping point fielder. Wilson runs to his left and cuts it off nicely. Two runs taken.
Root shuffles across and works it to mid-wicket.
Defended off the back foot by the batsman.
Straight again by McCarthy, Morgan turns it towards wide mid on where Chase dives to make a good stop. A run taken.
On a length on middle and leg, defended solidly off the back foot towards the bowler.
Slow through the air, eased down to long on for a run.
Tossed up on off, defended off the front foot.

SIX! Shot! Short delivery outside off, spinning in. Morgan goes deep in his crease and pulls it over deep mid-wicket for a maximum. When we talk about a short delivery troubling Morgan, certainly we don't mean from a spinner. He will hit those even in his sleep.
Floated around off, milked down to long off for a run.
Tossed up outside off, eased to sweeper cover for a run.
Quicker delivery outside off, stays a bit low. Morgan plays it with an angled bat to point.
Fullish ball on off, defended solidly.
Straying on the pads, clipped through square leg for a run.
Straight on this occasion, defended down the track.

FOUR! Well controlled! Here comes the short delivery, Morgan though stays composed and pulls it with authority over mid-wicket to earn himself a boundary. He was welcomed at the crease with a short delivery today and also fell in the last match attempting a hook shot. This time he handled it well.
The batsman rocks onto the back foot and punches the ball. One run added to the total.

Now the on air commentators (Ian Ward, Marcus Trescothick and Michael Atherton) are talking about Eoin Morgan's possible weakness. He got out pulling a short ball in the last ODI and was greeted today with a shorter one around his rib-cage by Barry McCarthy. But since then, the Irish bowlers have not tested him enough. Let's see whether McCarthy does that in this spell...
Back of a length outside off, Morgan strokes it to sweeper cover for a single.
Barry McCarthy is back on.
Floated on off, Root drives it towards Dockrell who dives to his left to deny him the run. Good work in the field by the Irishmen so far.
Shorter in length again, punched down to long on for an easy single.

Brilliant work, Balbirnie! Short delivery and sliding towards the pads, Root pulls it hard through mid-wicket and it is racing towards the fence. Andrew in the deep hares to his left and dives full length to save a certain boundary. Keeps it down to a single.
Root is finding the gaps at the moment! Turns this one to deep mid-wicket against the spin and runs swiftly to come back for the second.
Low full toss on middle, clipped to deep mid-wicket. The fielder is wide enough to allow the batsmen to come back for two runs.
Tossed up on off, eased back to the bowler.
Time for spin. George Dockrell to roll his arm over now.

Time for Drinks. A decent start for England. They have lost a couple of wickets but it has not slowed down proceedings. The runs continue to come easily and this is one area Ireland would like to address. Apart from picking wickets, they need to stop the run flow as well, because England bat deep.

FOUR! Clever from Morgan! The first slip was moved to gully before a few deliveries and he made perfect use of that.  On a good length outside off, angling in. Morgan waits for it and places it deftly past the keeper to get the desired result.
Good length delivery outside off, Root camps back and strokes it through covers for an easy run.
On a length outside off, punched off the back foot to sweeper cover for a run.
First slip moves to gully.
Fullish driven outside off, driven crisply but straight to extra cover.
Similar length delivery outside off, Eoin is cramped up for room a touch as he attempts to cut it. Gets no timing on it whatsoever and the ball rolls towards point.
Back of a length angling in from outside off, punched nicely off the back foot to sweeper cover for a couple.
Sliding down the leg side, Morgan deflects it off his pads to fine leg for one.
Around off on a shortish length, it's stroked from the back foot to sweeper cover for one.

Michael Atherton (on air) mentions about an area of vulnerability in Alex Hales' batting. He shows a couple of clips of his blazing cover drives and then shows a couple of deliveries in the line of the stumps. He did hit one boundary to them but got bowled in another one. Emphasizing that the bowlers should stick to wicket-to-wicket line against him and move the odd ball in as a surprising factor. Interesting point!
Pitches it full and outside off, Root plays a good looking square drive but finds the fielder.
Digs in a short ball on middle, Morgan stands tall and pulls it to deep mid-wicket for a single.
On a length and around middle, this time Morgan middles it nicely as he defends it down.
Takes a length ball away from the batsman, Eoin pushes at it from the crease and gets beaten.
Bowls it around off, Root punches it to the off side to end the over.
Shortish and in the line of the stumps, Morgan goes back and punches it square of the wicket on the off side for one.
The keeper comes up to the stumps as a result of the last shot.
SIX! Bang! Kevin bowls it full and outside off, angling in at a gentle pace, Morgan gives the charge and hoists it over the bowler's head for a maximum.
O'Brien switches to around the wicket and angles in a full ball on off, Morgan defends it off his front foot.
Back of a length delivery on off, defended to the off side.
Angles across a length delivery outside off, Morgan covers the line and shoulders arms.
Extra pace and bounce as it lands on a shortish length around off, Root shuffles across and pulls it down to fine leg for a couple of runs.
Back of a length ball around leg, Morgan moves across and nudges it down to fine leg for a run.
Eoin Morgan strides out to bat.

OUT! Great catch by Stirling, it was travelling at the speed of light! McCarthy delivers it on a length and outside off, Roy plays a blazing extra cover drive on the up and Stirling reacts quickly to hold on to a sharp catch. Barry is pumped up, another poor batting show by Jason. He is disappointed and walks back.
Shortish and outside off, punched to sweeper cover for one.
FOUR! Superb! Full in length and outside off, Root reaches out for it and creams it through cover-point for a boundary.
Fuller in length and on middle, driven firmly back to the bowler who made a good stop in his follow through.
Barry McCarthy is called into the attack.
Fullish and on the pads, this time it has been clipped away through mid-wicket for a single.
A touch short and outside off, tapped down to point.

Almost a catch to the cover fielder. O'Brien angles in a fuller length ball on middle and leg, Root leans forward and across to flick it off his pads but closes the face of the bat early. It pops out of the leading edge but dies down in front of the fielder at covers.
On middle and leg, clipped through mid-wicket for a single.
Straightens off the seam outside off, Roy feels for it and gets beaten.
FOUR! Lovely shot, Roy! A fractionally overpitched ball in the line of the stumps, Jason draws forward to cover the line and thumps it down the ground for a boundary.

Shout for an lbw! Movement off the surface for Murtagh, he pitches it on a good length outside off and gets it to nip back in. Root gets forward in defense but misses. He is hit on the pads, they appeal but the impact is outside off. Also, the replays detect some inside edge as well. Fine over.
Serves it full and outside off to the new batsman, Root who loves playing off the back foot is forced forward as he pushes it to the cover fielder.
Joe Root walks out to bat. Second slip comes in place for him.

OUT! Bowled 'em! Clever piece of bowling by Murtagh. He lands it on a length around off and the ball keeps on going with the angle after kissing the deck. Hales is on the back foot as he tries to defend, probably was thinking that the ball will move away off the seam. But it doesn't and goes right through his defense to destroy the stumps. Tim is delighted and so are his Irish teammates. Finally a success for the visiting team.
FOUR! Back and across trigger movement to a full ball around off, Hales checks the drive down the ground and fetches a boundary at long off. Beautifully played in the end.
Nearly edged it! Drops it on a length around off and shaping away, Hales pushes inside the line and misses.
On a length and outside off, Hales crouches and smacks his square cut. But he finds the point fielder.
Powerplay 2 has been signalled by the umpire. Four fielders are allowed outside the circle now.
Fractionally overpitched on off, driven to mid off.
The batsman has punched the ball off the back foot.
Good length ball outside off, Hales has a go at it. Gets it off the outer half down to third man. A run taken.
Fuller length ball outside off, Hales goes for a booming drive but gets it off the inner half down the track.
Fullish ball on middle, defended down the track.
Angling down the leg side, Hales looks to tickle it around the corner but fails to capitalize on it. The ball brushes his pads and rolls towards the keeper.
Kevin O'Brien has been introduced into the attack.

Cut into two halves! Length delivery outside off, shaping in sharply. Roy is foxed by the inswing and gets beaten to get hit on the flap of the front pad. The ball sails into the gloves of the keeper after that.
On a length on off, defended off the back foot to the off side.
Length delivery around off, Roy takes a couple of steps down the track and strokes it to mid off.
Fullish delivery around off, driven sweetly to extra cover.
On a length outside off, Roy camps back and pushes it to mid off.
Back of a length outside off, Roy runs it down to third man. The fielder hares to his left and cuts it off nicely. Two runs taken.
On a good length on middle, Hales covers the line and blocks it. 8 runs from that over.
Back of a length ball angling into Alex. He gets squared up a touch but manages to defend it to the off side.
Played to the mid-wicket region by the batsman.
FOUR! Dispatched with authority! Dug in short and it sits up nicely for Hales. He murders it past the short mid-wicket fielder for a rocketing boundary.
On a fuller length and shaping in sharply, Hales looks to defend it off the front foot tentatively but gets an inside edge onto his pads and the ball lands safely in the short mid-wicket region.
FOUR! Easy pickings! Dug in short outside off, Hales stands tall and has all the time in the world to pull it over mid-wicket to get the desired result.
Good length ball around off, Jason gets behind the line and defends it solidly.
Back of a length on middle, defended off the back foot solidly.
Short of a length and width on offer, Hales slashes at it hard but gets it off the outer half down to third man. A run taken.
On a length on off, pushed off the back foot past the right side of the bowler.
Second slip comes out.

On a fuller length just outside off, Hales comes forward and looks to block it tentatively. Gets an inside edge that hits his pads and lobs towards the vacant short leg region. Rarely you have a short leg in place in ODI cricket.
Good length delivery on off, Hales turns it through mid-wicket and picks up two runs for it.
Angling in from a length and it's too straight this time, clipped nicely to long leg for a couple.
On a length around off, shaping in. Roy shuffles a touch and pushes it to mid on.
FOUR! Beautiful shot! Back of a length ball outside off, Roy stands tall and punches it elegantly through extra cover. Has timed that to perfection and the ball whistles away to the fence.
Good length delivery nipping in sharply, Jason looks to tuck it through square leg but is hit on the thigh pad. No such appeal for an LBW as the impact was too high.
Fullish delivery around off, Roy drives it towards mid on. Didn't get it off the middle of the bat.
Wide! Chase gets his radar wrong and sprays it down the leg side, Jason looks to glance it but misses.
On a fuller length outside off, Roy eases it towards mid off. Porterfield dives to his right and makes a good save. Roy calls no loudly.
Pitches it full and just outside off, Alex defends it off his front foot to mid off. Good over by Murtagh!
A touch short and just around off, Hales gets back inside the crease and punches it straight to the cover fielder.
Full in length and on off, Hales gets back and punches it to covers.
Serves it on a length and outside off, shaping away, Hales watches the line closely after stepping down a bit and lets it through.
On a length around off, Roy walks forward with the flick shot and sends it to the fielder at deep mid-wicket for a single.
Fine leg comes up, mid-wicket drops back.
Fuller and on off, Hales closes the face of the bat and works it past mid-wicket for a single. The mid on fielder cuts it off.
Gets behind the line of the delivery and defends it towards mid on.
Lands it full and outside off, shaping back in a bit, Roy lunges and defends it with gentle hands to covers.
Fullish and angling in on middle, Roy presents a straight face and pushes it out to mid on.

Chase goes for a yorker but it reaches the batsman on a low full toss around middle, Hales clips it through square leg and the ball races through. Joyce runs across to his left from fine leg to make a sliding stop but cannot prevent three runs.
FOUR! You cannot bowl there to this batsman. He is particularly severe on anything full and wide outside off. Hales nails his extra cover drive for a boundary. No need to run for those!
Good length ball is angled into the batsman, it's around off and straightening a bit, Roy plays it with soft hands to mid-wicket and pinches a run.
On a good length and outside off, Hales decides very late to defend it towards covers.
Beauty by Murtagh! He slants in a full length ball around off and gets it to straighten just a touch, Hales gets forward to play the trajectory but is beaten.
Probes with a full length ball in the zone outside off, holding its line, Hales covers the line before shouldering arms.
Angles in a full ball on off, another gentle paced delivery, Hales presents a straight bat and pushes it back.
Fuller and on off, slower in pace, Roy pushes it with gentle hands to mid on and crosses for a single.
A touch short on off, defended off the back foot.

FOUR! Sublime! Not a good follow-up delivery by Peter. He bowls it on a length and outside off, Hales loves it there, takes a stride forward and drives it crisply through covers for a boundary. We saw a plenty of those shots in the last match.

Great delivery, Chase bends his back and generates some extra bounce around off, Hales tries playing from the front foot but is surprised by the lift. Does well eventually to keep it out safely but almost got into a tangle.
Hits the blockhole this time, Hales does well to dig it out towards covers.
Good length delivery in the region outside off, a hint of inward shape there but it's more after going past the batsman. Alex shoulders arms.

FOUR! Off the mark with a fine shot! Too full in length and on off, Hales brings down a straight bat and punches it past the diving mid on fielder for a boundary. It's down the slope and no stopping it from thereon.
Wide! A wild delivery, way down the leg side, an easy leave for the batsman and the keeper dives full length to his left to collect the ball.
Starts with a back of a length delivery outside off, Hales remains on the back foot and taps it down to point.
Peter Chase to bowl from the other end.
Another watchful front foot defense by Roy to complete the first over. A good one by Tim!
Fullish on off, moving back in, Roy defends it to the leg side.
FOUR! Great shot to get off the mark! Murtagh in search for extra movement overpitches it around off, Jason strides forward and plays an eye-catching straight drive for a boundary.
On a good length and outside off, shaping away a touch, Roy feels for it and gets beaten. Tidy lines!

Appeal for an lbw! Murtagh who has a good experience of playing in England, brings a length ball back into the batsman this time. Roy with a tentative front foot movement tries to defend but misses. He is hit high on the pads, they appeal but the umpire disagrees. There was some sound indicating the involvement of an inside edge but the replays detect nothing. It shows that the noise was of the bat brushing the front pad. Anyway, it's too high and the right decision was made.
Starts with a decent length ball around off, Roy gets forward and defends it to the off side. Watchful from Jason, he bagged a duck in the previous game.
We are ready to get underway. Jason Roy and Alex Hales to open the batting for England. Tim Murtagh to take the new ball for Ireland. Two slips in place. Here we go...
England (Playing XI) - Jason Roy, Alex Hales, Joe Root, Eoin Morgan(c), Jonny Bairstow, Sam Billings(w), Adil Rashid, David Willey, Liam Plunkett, Jake Ball, Mark Wood.
Ireland (Playing XI) - Ed Joyce, Paul Stirling, William Porterfield(c), Andrew Balbirnie, Niall O'Brien(w), Gary Wilson, Kevin O'Brien, Barry McCarthy, George Dockrell, Tim Murtagh, Peter Chase.
Toss - Ireland win the toss and opt to bowl. One change for the visitors. BARRY MCCARTHY comes in for Stuart Thompson. On the other hand, England remain unchanged.

The tourists do not have the best of techniques against spin and the home side will look to make life difficult for them once again. England are looking in good shape before the ICC Champions Trophy and will look to build on their strengths. They have one of the most explosive batting line-ups in world cricket and their variety in bowling is a force to reckon with. Can the hosts clinch the series 2-0 or will the Irishmen come back hard to prove their mettle?

Hello and a warm welcome for the second and final ODI between England and Ireland at the Lord's. Grey skies welcome us in London and it will be a stern test for the batsmen against the moving ball. This is the first game for Ireland against England at the Home of Cricket and they will be eager to make this a memorable affair after a lackluster show in the last match. They have plenty to ponder upon but they rather need to execute their skills immediately and bring their A game to the fore.
